data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic word 'tul' meaning rain and 'ibn' meaning son. This name is a symbol of divine blessings and is often given to a child born during a rainy season.

data.cultural_impact: The name Tulaib signifies a connection to the natural world and the cycle of life, particularly the renewal brought by rain. It is a name deeply rooted in Islamic culture, reminding us of Allah's (SWT) promise of blessings and new beginnings (Surah Al-Qamar 54:1).
data.spiritual_significance: Tulaib is a sacred name that evokes a sense of hope, renewal, and blessings from Allah (SWT). It serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in Allah (SWT) and His timing. The name invites a deep appreciation for the smaller blessings in life, like the rain, while eliciting thoughts of the greater blessings in aspects of life like a newborn baby boy.

historical_references.reference: The Prophet Muhammad is reported to have planted a palm tree in Madinah named 'Tulaib' in the year 632 CE. It is said that the tree bore fruit only during his lifetime.
historical_references.context: During the Prophet Muhammad's time in Madinah.

historical_references.reference: Tulaib ibn Rib'i, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, was given the title 'Asad al-Anam' (Lion of the People) due to his bravery and strength during the Battle of Uhud in 625 CE. The tree may have been named after him due to his nickname.
historical_references.context: During the time of the early Islamic conquests.
